samples.identification: SultanLauncher.exe 0.0.0.0, .NET Framework WPF Minecraft 1.21.4 cheat-client launcher
samples.reason: The examined executable implements an overt game launcher and licensing client. Its anti-debug capabilities are real but no unauthorized payload, theft, persistence, or remote-command path was established. This is an artifact-scoped judgment for sighted quarantine, not an endorsement of its distribution or missing game payload.
execution_paths: Entry token 0x06000002 (RVA 0x211c): initialize launcher_debug.txt, exception handlers, WPF application and MainWindow. Constructor RVA 0x23d0 builds the UI; no anti-debug helper invocation.
ComputeHWID RVA 0x71e0 reads C: volume serial, MachineName, UserName and ProcessorCount, hashes the concatenation with MD5 and formats the first eight bytes for licensing.

Login event -> PerformServerLogin async state machine -> QueryAuthServer RVA 0x4258. POSTs explicitly entered launcher login/password and licensing HWID to loopback /api/auth/login, then configured myjino PHP endpoint. Falls back to local website/users.json, checks password/subscription/HWID and can persist first HWID binding. No Microsoft/Minecraft token or unrelated secret-store acquisition.
HttpPostJson RVA 0x45e0 creates HttpWebRequest, sets POST and JSON content type, writes the serialized login data, reads a JSON authentication response; no response-to-code activation.
DeployRunFilesToDriveC RVA 0x6204 copies adjacent run/{mods,config,Sultan} and options.txt into roaming AppData/.sultan. CopyDir RVA 0x6354 recurses locally.

StartLaunch async MoveNext RVA 0x63f8 verifies subscription, deploys game files, animates progress then launches adjacent start.ps1 (or ../start.ps1) via powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File. Arguments carry nickname, RAM, role, UID, subscription, HWID, and -Guard active. UseShellExecute=false, CreateNoWindow=true. The UI injection messages are status text; no process injection is performed by this path.
Other Process.Start calls open registration/cabinet pages through the configured handler.

ErasePEHeaderInMemory RVA 0x6f98, CheckForHooks RVA 0x7014, HideCurrentThread RVA 0x70c0, CheckForDebuggers RVA 0x70f8, and CheckBlacklistedProcesses RVA 0x714c have no call/ldftn references in this assembly. Their bodies respectively zero the first 4096 module bytes, inspect ntdll debugger entry bytes for 0xCC/0xE9, request thread information class 17, inspect debugger state, and scan process names against analyst-tool names. Their presence still warrants the retained suspicious thread-hiding trait.
LoadImageFromDataOrUrl RVA 0x2700 decodes Base64 image data or supplies a URI to BitmapImage; the result is displayed, not executed. No additional string obfuscation was found.

packaging.authenticode: No security directory or signature record; independently checked with PE parsing and osslsigncode. There is no signer whose integrity can be asserted.
packaging.resources: Avatar 964400 bytes and Banner1/Banner2 1275624 bytes each: CRC-checked PNG chunks ending exactly at IEND; no appended resource trailers. No PE overlay. Images explain most .text/whole-file entropy; the accurate entropy traits are retained.
packaging.managed_dependencies: Framework UI, IO, HTTP, JSON and cryptography assemblies; no embedded managed dependency or executable resource.

samples.provenance_and_limits: MalwareBazaar listing redirected to a generic unavailable/detail page; no family or abuse context was recovered. Unsigned cheat-launcher packaging, anti-debug helper code, SuppressIldasm, hidden PowerShell launch and high-entropy image resources plausibly explain collection/heuristic labeling. This explanation is inference, not a recovered source attribution. Adjacent start.ps1, run files, website database and original deployment context were not supplied. The configured public auth host failed DNS resolution during forager retrieval; no server behavior is invented.

samples.reason: The exact original archive is an inert placeholder: only a 163-byte package.json and 19-byte README. No executable code, lifecycle hook, dependency, entry point or referenced URL. Installing these bytes cannot execute the later release beacon.
samples.packaging: tar member table checked directly; no links, hidden executable members, or additional data. A separately recovered npmmirror copy is SHA-256 identical and its SHA-1/SHA-512 agree with registry dist metadata.
samples.why_reported: GHSA-hcw5-m6mm-qg3q applies to all versions (>=0). The registry records nine releases within minutes, an internal-looking scope, and later 0.0.1/1.0.1/3.0.0/99.0.1/2.0.0/2.0.1/1.1.0 releases with postinstall=node beacon.cjs. Recovered 0.0.1 actually POSTs package name, hostname, installPath, cwd and Node version to a public IP. Its malicious install-beacon traits remain hostile. This supports campaign/package-level labeling, not executable behavior in 0.1.0.
samples.provenance_and_limits: Current top-level maintainer is npm-support while historical 0.1.0 publisher/maintainer is kibt. The unlisted-publisher finding reflects present-versus-historical custody drift; no prior owner or actual account takeover is established. Malicious siblings are contextual controls, not dependencies or members of this archive. No broad exemption for this package name was added.

changes: Guard/no-guard token descriptions no longer infer watchdog behavior; matchers/severities and the Guardian consumer are unchanged.

WPF UI/helper name atomic YARA fingerprints require both the name and independent WPF-framework evidence in .text and describe references, not invocation. Generic game-mod groups moved to the WPF library home; Endfield and the Cobalt/IcedID consumer references were updated. Name-only strings without WPF no longer identify that library. Existing WPF-constrained consumers retain their tested matching populations.

HWID/localAppHWID exact-name observations moved from analytics to hardware-information labels, preserving matchers, scope, severity and consumers. Their union lives in sysinfo/profile so a hardware-directory threshold cannot count that group and its atomic source twice. Bare labels prove neither a query nor telemetry. Audited hardware/sysinfo parent consumers: two profile thresholds and Perl/OOB predicates; no unsupported new result appeared in the batch or one-label controls.

Fresh unlisted publisher composite moved from the takeover/impersonation objective to metadata/registry, keeping its conditions and notable severity. Removed unsupported takeover wording and ATT&CK mapping; [all] is the registry leaf's OS-independent platform contract.
consumer_audit: All exact references and ancestor directory selectors inspected. No ancestor selectors consume the moved game-mod/WPF or registry-publish sets. The one well-known/lib exclusion targets ELF while these WPF rules target PE. HWID exact consumers updated in general-telemetry and activity-exfiltration; parent consumers checked with controls. Original source-file inventories are recorded separately.
remaining_disagreements: Both deployed ML classifications remain BENIGN (cls=0, calibrated level=-1); raw model scores changed without tuning for a desired verdict. One suspicious thread-hide capability remains on the BENIGN launcher because verdict and capability severity are independent. External malware labels disagree with these artifact-specific judgments for the reasons above. No hostile detection was lost on the recovered beacon or consumer controls.

checks.wpf_name_only_control: Only unsupported WPF identity removed; debug/thread-hide and other supported detections retained.
checks.cobalt_icedid_consumer_control: Existing hostile composite fires before and after on the same admin/WPF/two-embedded-header evidence. This is a static rule-consumer control, not a genuine malware specimen.
checks.native_endfield_controls: Official v5.1.1 and v2.1.1 binaries and their embedded members compared before/after; all existing findings including hostile capability composites retained. They are native controls, not WPF positives and have not been adjudicated as task samples.
checks.validator_format_correction: The first full validation rejected inline primitives in composites. These were converted to atomic WPF/name YARA fingerprints; all comparison checks were repeated.
checks.scan_environment: Initial installed validator rejected an already documented 101-rule naming budget. Atomscan rescans used CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0 and --no-update. Final validation uses the named newer Cleave build with that reviewed budget; no unrelated rules were deleted. Model bundle warns v18 features lag extractor v19; this limits interpretation of scores.
